newsitem.title: USA: NAPM index falls in January, manufacturing growth slows.
newsitem.headline: NAPM index falls in January, manufacturing growth slows.

text.p: U.S. manufacturing activity grew at a slower rate in January than in December, even though the overall economy continued to expand for the 69th month in a row, the National Association of Purchasing Management said on Monday.
The industry group for the nation's purchasing executives, who buy wholesale supplies for factories, said its index of maufacturing activity fell to 52.0 in January from a revised 53.8 in December.
Wall Street economists polled by Reuters had expected a 53.0 reading. A level above 50 signals growth, while a reading below 50 points to economic sluggishness.
The surprisingly big drop suggests the manufacturing sector will likely slow down in the first quarter after a strong fourth quarter in 1996, analysts said.
"We're going to get some more tempered type of numbers," said Michael Strauss, chief economist at Sanwa Securities (USA) Co.
Still, he said, "the numbers signal very few price pressures from the factory sector. It seems to imply that price pressures will be somewhat limited."
NAPM's price index in January crept up to 51.4 percent from 50.8 percent, reflecting higher prices for a second consecutive month.
NAPM's employment index rose to 48.7 percent from 47.5 percent, but stayed below 50 percent, showing that manufacturing jobs fell for the 23rd month in a row but at a slower rate.

"Purchasing executives' comments on business conditions in January were less optimistic than in December, with many members describing business conditions as stable," said Norbert Ore, who chairs the NAPM's Business Survey Committee and is a director of purchasing at Sonoco Products Co.
"Prices paid were higher, but were not noted as a particular concern to members. Employment continued to decline, but at a slower rate."
NAPM's production index fell to 58.1 percent from 58.5 in December. Its new orders index slid to 53.5 percent from 58.2 percent.
Backlog of orders lost ground for the sixth time in seven months during January, with the index dropping to 45.5 percent from 51 percent in December.
NAPM's supplier deliveries index in January rose to 48.5 percent from 51.6 percent, signalling faster deliveries. Its inventories index slowed to 44.4 percent from 44.9 percent.

Asked about customers' inventories of products, 11 percent of purchasing executives felt they were too high, down from 16 percent in December. But 18 percent felt they were too low, up from 17 percent in December, while those who thought they were about right rose to 71 percent from 67 percent in December.

NAPM's new export orders index fell to 54.6 percent, but remained above 50 percent for the 11th month in a row. Imports of materials by manufacturers fell as NAPM's imports index moved down to 51.8 percent from 52.7 percent in December.

Of the 20 manufacturing industries, eight reported an improvement in January. These include petroleum; chemicals; apparel; jewelry, toys, sporting goods, musical instruments; industrial and commercial equipment and computers; electronic components and equipment; leather; transportation; textiles; and instruments and photographic equipment.
